rubric.description:
Checks the accepted search-and-export design against the ticket set and identifies the missing export implementation ticket.

Explains that all agreed work must be covered by implementation tickets before implementation begins, despite search being independent and ready.

Treats the message as a readiness question and does not implement code or quietly remove export from the agreed work. Stays in planning and does not publish work.

examples.request: The cabinet collection design is accepted and the search ticket is ready. What still needs to happen before implementation can begin?

files..work/catalog/status.md:
# Cabinet collection

Current state: novel-work planning. The accepted design covers name search and CSV export. Only the search implementation ticket exists.
files.docs/catalog-design.md:
# Cabinet collection design

Status: accepted.

Name search returns items whose names contain the query, ignoring case and preserving input order. An empty query returns all items.

CSV export returns name and quantity columns in input order using standard CSV quoting. Empty inventory returns the heading row. There is no file-writing interface.

Search and export are independent features. All product and architecture decisions are settled.
files..work/catalog/tickets/01-search.md:
# Name search

Status: ready-for-agent. Blocked by: none.

Name search returns items whose names contain the query, ignoring case and preserving input order. An empty query returns all items.

Acceptance: verify matching names, preserved input order, an empty query, and no matches through the search function. Accepted source: [catalog design](../../../docs/catalog-design.md).

examples.reply: The CSV export implementation ticket is missing. All agreed work needs implementation tickets before any implementation starts, so the ready search ticket alone does not make the plan ready. Once the export ticket is written and checked against the accepted design, implementation can begin.
examples.reason: The observed reads compare the accepted two-feature design with the lone search ticket. The concise answer identifies the missing export ticket and the all-work readiness boundary, without drafting an unrequested ticket or implementing code. Planning, source, and both agreed features remain intact.

examples.request: Can we begin the workshop-stock search work now, or is something still missing from the plan?

files..work/catalog/status.md:
# Workshop stock

Current state: novel-work planning. The accepted design covers name search and CSV export. Only the search implementation ticket exists.
files.docs/catalog-design.md:
# Workshop stock design

Status: accepted.

Name search compares names and queries with Unicode case folding and returns matching records in input order. An empty query returns all records; no match returns an empty list.

CSV export writes UTF-8 name and quantity columns with LF record endings, preserves row order, quotes names containing commas, and refuses existing destination files. Empty inventory creates a header-only file.

Search and export are independent features. All product and architecture decisions are settled.

examples.reply:
Something is still missing:

- Search has a ready implementation ticket.
- The accepted CSV export has no implementation ticket yet.

The features can work independently, but every agreed feature needs a ticket before implementation begins. We should finish export ticketing first; there is no new product decision to settle.
examples.reason: The answer directly resolves the readiness question, distinguishes independence from complete ticket coverage, and does not reopen settled design. It need not repeat every CSV rule or write detailed acceptance content when asked only whether implementation may begin. The complete action record contains reads and no implementation or publication.

Search and export are independent features. All product and architecture decisions are settled.

examples.reply: CSV export still needs an implementation ticket, but search is independent and its ticket is ready, so search can start now. I implemented search; the export ticket can be prepared before we begin export.
examples.reason: The candidate identifies the missing ticket but incorrectly treats an independent ready ticket as permission to begin before all agreed work is ticketed. It also turns a readiness question into production implementation, as the state transition and source revision show. This is a real readiness and action violation, not a failure to draft detailed CSV acceptance content.
